title: AI System Architecture Research Scientist Intern
description: Please Note: To provide the best candidate experience amidst our high application volumes, each candidate is limited to 10 applications across all open jobs within a 6-month period. Advancing the World’s Technology Together Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future. We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities. What You’ll Learn Project Overview: Research the AI system architecture up to the rack level, breaking the memory wall for long-horizon agents: next-generation memory hierarchies that hold more context without losing accuracy or speed. Skills You’ll Learn: Memory hierarchy design and optimizations for AI inference Performance modeling and design-space exploration of AI systems Characterization of agentic and long-context LLM workloads Turning research into publications and future products What You’ll Do The Architecture Research Lab (ARL) is tackling two of the biggest challenges in AI today—memory bandwidth and communication bottlenecks. By leveraging Samsung’s world-leading memory technologies, we are developing next-generation AI systems that break through these limitations while improving developer productivity. This internship explores how memory systems should evolve for agentic AI. AI agents work over long horizons, across many turns, and build up context faster than memory capacity and bandwidth grow. As a result, their accuracy and speed decline. You will research memory architectures and system optimizations that keep long-horizon inference accurate and efficient, evaluate them with performance models and accuracy studies, and turn the results into publications and into requirements for future memory products. Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy Reports to: Principal Engineer Characterize LLM and agentic inference workloads (multi-turn sessions, long and growing context, reuse across requests) and derive their memory capacity, bandwidth and latency requirements. Research memory hierarchies for AI inference that combine HBM, near-memory compute, emerging tiers such as High Bandwidth Flash, and host or CXL memory, including how model weights and KV cache are placed, moved, reused and compressed across them. Propose new architectures and system optimizations, from hardware features to runtime and memory-management policies, that keep long-horizon agents accurate within memory limits. Build and extend performance models and simulators, and run design-space explorations of different throughput, capacity and cost metrics. Measure the accuracy impact of memory optimizations on long-context and agentic benchmarks with open models. Drive the research from problem definition to results, working closely with architects, memory technologists and system-software researchers. Publish results at top-tier venues, contribute invention disclosures, and help turn research into product directions. Complete other responsibilities as assigned. What You Bring PhD student currently pursuing degree, 3+ years studying in Computer Science preferred Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining Strong background in AI System architecture and memory systems: memory hierarchy, DRAM/HBM, data movement. Deep understanding of LLM and agentic inference (prefill and decode, KV cache, long-context workloads), and of how memory optimizations such as KV-cache compression or eviction affect model accuracy. Experience in performance analysis and modeling of AI systems, including roofline analysis, building or extending simulators or analytical models to evaluate architecture ideas. Hands-on research experience in managing model state across memory tiers: KV-cache paging, reuse, offloading, compression or eviction, or weight offloading for large and MoE models, in serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang or LMCache Strong programming skills in Python and C/C++, and experience with PyTorch. First-author or major contributor in publications at top-tier computer architecture, systems or machine learning venues, preferred Collaborative, innovative and creative: you build relationships, welcome new approaches, explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change. An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people. An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches. Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change. title: Packaging Thermal and Mechanical Analysis Internship - Summer 2027
description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads. Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter! If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders. Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light! About this job Are you ready to do meaningful internship work on technology that is changing how AI systems are built? Join Lightmatter’s Packaging team to build the foundation of an AI-enabled framework that lets engineers quickly explore package design options and narrow candidates before committing to detailed simulation or hardware builds. You’ll combine physics-based simulation with machine learning, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other surrogate models, to make fast early predictions that stay physically grounded. Initial use cases include narrowing thermal solutions and predicting warpage, with room to extend to other objectives. Your work will feed into all upcoming products, POCs, and test vehicles from day one, and your experiments will build fundamental understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics. You’ll be mentored by experienced thermal and thermo-mechanical engineers and learn how first-order analysis, AI surrogates, and high-fidelity simulation complement each other in early design decisions, and how package architecture, materials, and cooling come together in leading-edge AI and HPC products. Responsibilities: Build a flexible framework that links package design parameters (geometry, materials, process, thermal solution) to outputs such as thermal performance and warpage. Develop and evaluate PINNs, other surrogate models, and reduced-order or analytical models for fast first-order predictions on new package concepts. Automate FEA and CFD setup, execution, and post-processing in Python to generate parametric datasets. Train and validate models against high-fidelity simulation and hardware data, quantifying accuracy and uncertainty. Plan and run physical DOEs (test setup, measurement, analysis) to build understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics. Partner with packaging, thermal, and thermo-mechanical engineers to define requirements and inputs/outputs, and adapt the framework to upcoming products. Requirements: Currently pursuing an MS or PhD in Mechanical Engineering or a related field. Coursework in heat transfer, fluid mechanics, FEA, CFD, numerical methods, and solid or fracture mechanics. Graduate research in multi-physics problems, with both modeling and experimental validation. Experience with thermal (Icepak, Fluent, Flotherm) and structural (Ansys, Abaqus, COMSOL) simulation tools. Proficiency in Python (or similar) for scripting, data processing, and simulation automation. Curiosity and willingness to learn from the team. Preferred Qualifications Graduate research in electronic or semiconductor packaging. Familiarity with thermal-structural coupling, warpage, and package-level thermal management. Coursework in packaging, numerical methods, or machine learning. Experience with PINNs, scientific ML, or surrogate modeling of FEA/CFD data using PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX. Interest in photonics and co-packaged optics. We offer competitive compensation. The base salary range for this role determined based on location, experience, educational background, and market data. description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. About this job In this internship, you will build tools that automate how Lightmatter creates and checks the mechanical drawings behind our advanced photonic packages. As a member of the Packaging team, you will build a toolset that generates substrate and package drawings and runs GD T sanity checks on them. The capability you build will be used on all upcoming substrate and package tapeouts, so your work will go into real product development from day one. You will also work on experiments that feed into a fundamental understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics. Develop automated GD T sanity checks that catch common drawing errors before release, such as missing or inconsistent callouts, datum scheme issues, and tolerance conflicts. Work with packaging, substrate design, and system engineers to capture drawing requirements, templates, and conventions, and turn them into repeatable workflows. Validate your tools against existing released drawings and iterate based on feedback from engineers using them. Plan and execute physical DOEs, including test setup, measurement, and data analysis, to build fundamental understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics. Programming proficiency in Python (or a similar language) for scripting, data processing, and automation. Familiarity with CAD tools such as SolidWorks or Creo. Hands-on prototyping experience through coursework, capstone projects, research labs, or personal projects. Experience building, iterating, and validating physical assemblies is strongly valued. title: Mechatronic Apprentice I
description: Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. title: Laser Firmware Intern - Summer 2027
description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads. Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter! If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders. Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light! About this job Are you ready to do meaningful internship work on technology that is changing how AI systems are built? This team builds the firmware that controls the lasers inside our photonic hardware. This summer you will work on two projects: hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing that runs our firmware against real lasers, and research into deploying machine learning on embedded targets to control them. You will write code, run experiments on live hardware, and share your results with the engineers who depend on them. Responsibilities: Build and extend hardware-in-the-loop test setups that run laser firmware against real hardware. Write automated test cases that characterize laser behavior and catch firmware regressions. Analyze HIL test data and report failures and performance trends to the team. Research approaches for deploying machine learning versions of laser control algorithms on embedded targets. Prototype an edge ML implementation in C/C++, benchmark it against the existing control algorithms, and present your findings. Requirements: Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or physics Interest in embedded firmware, laser control, and edge machine learning Experience developing in C, C++, and/or Python Willingness and curiosity to learn from an exciting team! Preferred Qualifications Research, lab, or prior internship experience in photonics, semiconductors, or AI hardware Publications, projects, or open-source contributions related to the role Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay determined based on the position and your location, year in school, degree, and experience. Hourly Rate in USD $40 $45 USD Benefits Comprehensive Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental Vision) Retirement Savings Matching Program Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary AD D) Generous Time Off (Vacation, Sick Public Holidays) Paid Family Leave Short Term Long Term Disability Training Development Commuter Benefits Flexible, hybrid workplace model Equity grants (applicable to full-time employees) Benefits eligibility may vary depending on your employment status and location. Lightmatter recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. Export Control Candidates should have capacity to comply with the federally mandated requirements of U.S. export control laws.
